note: THEMES FOR CREATORS. Tyler, 2026-08-23: 'Set → how many cards → theme → narrow it down. We should be sparking their brain for them. Give them inspiration and they'll never leave.' A search box is a tool; a funnel is fuel. · card-text themes derive membership by reading attackNames, captured 2026-08-23.
slopRule: Every theme is EITHER derived from a field we hold (artist, setId, rarity, releaseDate) OR a NAMED LIST stored right here where anybody can argue with it. 'Cute' is not in the data — but eighteen specific baby Pokémon are, and a list can be disagreed with where an adjective cannot. That is the whole difference between curation and slop.
framing: Themes needing taste are framed as SELECTION, never as ranking. 'Nine cute cards for your binder' invites you to disagree; 'the nine cutest cards' tells you that you are wrong. A question gets replies and replies are the game.

themes.name: Pokémon that are food
themes.hook: Which one would you actually eat?
themes.why: Nobody expects a themed page of edible Pokémon and everybody has an opinion about Vanilluxe.

themes.name: The baby Pokémon
themes.hook: Which page is going in the front of the binder?
themes.why: A real category with a real boundary — these are the pre-evolutions introduced from Gen II onward, not a mood.

themes.name: Ghost-type nightmares
themes.hook: Which one actually scared you as a kid?
themes.why: Ghost art is where artists are given the most room, and it shows.

themes.name: Pokémon caught napping
themes.hook: Late night check-in. Who's still awake?
themes.why: Proved: the cropped Charmander post using this register did 791 views against a data post's 154, same account, same week.
themes.note: Widened 2026-08-23. Seven strictly-sleeping Pokemon produced three art-safe credited cards, which is a coincidence rather than a theme. Tired is a MOOD - Slowpoke and Slakoth are not asleep, they just look the way 2am feels, and that is the post. Merged with late-night 2026-08-23 — the two were the same theme written twice, found by the duplicate check rather than by reading.

themes.name: One artist, across the years
themes.basis: artist field + earliest and latest hero card
themes.hook: {years} years apart. Same artist.
themes.why: The shape that landed first — Base Set Charizard beside the 151 Blastoise ex.

themes.name: One Pokémon, many artists
themes.hook: {n} artists. One {mon}. Which is the definitive one?
themes.why: The differences argue for themselves and the post needs no words.

themes.name: The same trio, across eras
themes.basis: a named trio + releaseDate + rarity, three complete sets
themes.hook: Which row wins?
themes.why: Three eras stacked as rows. It asks rather than tells, which is what gets a reply instead of a scroll.

themes.name: Cards with a story
themes.basis: a sourced fact from data/knowledge.json plus the card it names
themes.hook: Most people have no idea this happened.
themes.why: Kadabra vanished from the card game for twenty-one years because a man who bends spoons sued. Every claim carries a source and a falsifier.

themes.name: The best of one set
themes.hook: Six from {set}. Which page are you filling first?
themes.why: Works for anybody currently opening that set, which is most people most of the time.

themes.name: An artist's debut
themes.hook: Everybody starts somewhere.
themes.why: A debut is a date in the data, not a judgment — and the contrast with their best-known work does the rest.

themes.name: Card battle
themes.basis: same Pokemon, comparable value, different artist or era
themes.hook: {mon}. {setA} or {setB}? No wrong answer, but you have one.
themes.why: A battle only works if it is CLOSE. A $2,000 card against a $12 one is not a debate, it is a price check with a question mark on it. Candidates are matched within 45% on value so nobody can settle it by pointing at a number - which forces an actual opinion, and an opinion is a reply.

themes.name: What actually happened
themes.basis: a sourced fact from data/knowledge.json with a falsifier attached
themes.hook: Most people have no idea this happened.
themes.why: Controversy is the one topic where being wrong costs the most, so nothing here is remembered - it is cited or it is not published. Being wrong about a controversy is how you become one.

themes.name: The pseudo-legendaries
themes.hook: Which one did you actually raise?
themes.why: 600 base stat total, three-stage line, always a 1,250,000 EXP grind. Every player has one they put the hours into.

themes.name: The mythicals
themes.hook: How many of these did you actually get legitimately?
themes.why: Event-only distribution means most people never had them in-game. The cards are how a lot of players first saw them.

themes.name: Revived from fossils
themes.hook: Which fossil did you pick, and do you regret it?
themes.why: A forced choice in every game that has them, and people remember which they took twenty years later.

themes.name: Cat Pokémon
themes.hook: Which one is going in the binder?
themes.why: Cat art gets more personality than almost any other category, and everybody has a favourite for reasons they cannot defend.

themes.name: Dog Pokémon
themes.hook: Cats or dogs. Pick a side.
themes.why: Pairs directly against the cat page, which is the argument.

themes.name: The regional birds
themes.hook: Every game gives you one. Which was yours?
themes.why: Every generation has an early-route bird nobody thinks about until they see them lined up.

themes.name: Ice types
themes.hook: Which one belongs on a winter page?
themes.why: Ice art leans on light and texture more than any other type, and it reads beautifully in a grid.

themes.name: The starters
themes.hook: First pick, every time. Which one?
themes.why: The single most universal Pokémon memory there is. Everybody chose.

themes.name: Dragon types
themes.hook: Which dragon actually looks the part?
themes.why: The type people chase hardest, and the art usually knows it.

themes.name: Sun and water
themes.hook: Which page are you taking to the beach?
themes.why: A mood rather than a type, and the grid does the work.

themes.name: Mega Evolutions
themes.hook: Which mega deserved to come back?
themes.why: Gone for years, then back in 2025. Everybody has one they missed.

openQuestions: Aesthetically pleasing has no honest basis yet. Rarity is a proxy for effort, not for beauty, and we should not pretend otherwise. It needs either a stored list somebody stands behind or a community vote — and a vote would be better content than our opinion anyway.
Type-based themes (all Water, all Dragon) would be easy and are not in our data — the catalogue has no type field. Worth adding if a source has it.
shapeRule: Every theme declares a SHAPE and the editor dispatches on it. Dispatching on id meant four themes produced silently nothing and two shared a branch and returned identical results. A theme without a shape now fails visibly instead of quietly.
groupRule: Themes are GROUPED, not disclosed. 35 chips in one row is a wall — the research is explicit that a set this size needs structure rather than a more-options click, because hiding a core control is friction dressed as minimalism.
